Fix: revert db_pool_max to 50 and exclude payments from the cost-optimizer's pool-shrinking.

summaries:
# ShopCo On-Call Rotation Summary (days 1–12, through Fri 2026-09-11 03:17)

## Architecture reminder
web → checkout + search; checkout → payments (→ external provider) + inventory; payments & inventory → Postgres; search → Redis. Metrics table has one row/service/minute incl. `postgres` and `redis` rows; `db_conn_in_use` is the *client pool* gauge on payments/inventory (Postgres row's own conns are separate and normally ~6–11).

## Pages closed

**p-001 … p-013 (except p-005) — the nightly inventory_p99_high. ALL DISMISSED as noise.**
- Symptom, every single night at 03:02: `inventory_p99_high` fires, value ~1000–1300ms (baseline ~110–130ms). Auto-resolves at 03:14 with value back to ~108–131ms.
- Root cause: scheduled `inventory-batch` reindex job. Logs show `reindex job started` at exactly 03:00:00 and `reindex job completed in 12m` at 03:12:00. Postgres CPU jumps ~30% → 72–86%, Postgres `db_conn_in_use` ~8 → 35–52 for the duration. Inventory p99 returns to normal the same minute the job completes.
- NOT a deploy/config incident: it occurred on day 1 before any deploys existed, and on day 7 (Sun 2026-09-06) with **zero deploys and zero config changes the prior day** — that's the cleanest proof. Ruled out dep-001…dep-027 and cfg-001…cfg-011 on the grounds that the spike is identical on nights with and without changes.
- No customer impact ever: inventory `error_rate` stays ~0.001, `rps` flat (~22.5 weekday, ~13.5 weekend), inventory's own CPU ~30%, and web/checkout/search/payments all at baseline in the window.
- Pages: p-001 (d1), p-002 (d2), p-003 (d3), p-004 (d4), p-006 (d5), p-007 (d6), p-008 (d7), p-009 (d8), p-010 (d9), p-011 (d10), p-012 (d11), p-013 (d12). Twelve dismissals.
- **Open action item I have escalated in every dismissal and which the day team has still not actioned: add a 03:00–03:15 maintenance suppression for `inventory_p99_high`, or make the alert batch-aware.**

**p-005 (day 4, Thu 2026-09-03 11:36) — REAL INCIDENT. Resolved with cfg-004.**
- Symptom: cascade of four alerts — checkout_error_rate_high (0.0377) 11:36, web_error_rate_high (0.0237) 11:41, payments_p99_high (2056) 11:46, checkout_p99_high (2034) 11:48.
- Root cause: **cfg-004** at 02:00, `cost-optimizer-bot` cut `payments.db_pool_max` 50 → 20. Harmless overnight; as morning traffic ramped (payments 15→80 rps) in-use conns went 4→11→18 and **pinned at the ceiling ~20** from ~11:20. Payments then logged `request timed out after 3000ms waiting for db connection` (precursor at 11:15: `slow db acquire: waited 387ms`). Payments p99 280ms→2000ms+, error_rate 0.001→0.135.
- Downstream, not separate failures: checkout `payment authorization failed: upstream payments timeout after 3000ms`, web `POST /checkout returned 502 from upstream checkout`.
- Ruled out: **dep-008** (checkout v1.4.2 "tweak retry logging", 11:16) — tempting by timing but it only touched logging and errors originate *in payments*. Ruled out Postgres itself — server-side conns ~10, p99 <11ms, i.e. the bottleneck was the client pool cap, not the DB.
- Fixed by cfg-005 (12:40, alice) reverting db_pool_max 20 → 50.

## Recurring patterns / heuristics that paid off
1. **The 03:02 inventory page is noise.** Recognition signature (3 cheap queries, ~1 min): (a) logs 02:50→now showing `inventory-batch reindex job started` 03:00 / `completed in 12m` 03:12; (b) one GROUP BY service aggregate over 03:00–03:17 (min/max p99, avg+max error_rate, avg rps, max conns, max cpu) showing only inventory p99 elevated and everything else flat; (c) alerts table showing the auto-resolve at 03:14. If all three match, dismiss. **If any of them differs — job missing/longer than 12m, error_rate rising, another service degraded, or no auto-resolve by 03:14 — treat as real and dig.**
2. **`cost-optimizer-bot` config changes at 02:00 are the highest-risk events on this system.** Pattern: shrink a capacity limit at 02:00, looks fine at overnight traffic, breaks at the weekday 10:00–12:00 ramp. Known instances: cfg-004 (payments.db_pool_max 50→20 — caused p-005), cfg-007 (checkout.worker_threads 16→12, day 7 — survived Monday peak fine), cfg-009 (web.cache_ttl_s 60→45, day 9 — no ill effect, search cache_hit_rate stayed ~0.915), cfg-010 (redis.maxmemory_mb 4096→3584, day 10 — overnight fine, cache_hit_rate 0.917, redis p99 ~1.7ms; **has not yet been proven at a weekday peak — check search/redis cache_hit_rate and eviction during 10:00–12:00**).
3. **Saturation signature to look for**: a service's `db_conn_in_use` flat-lining at a round number = pool ceiling; pair with logs containing `waiting for db connection` / `slow db acquire`.
4. **Follow errors upstream to their origin service.** web 502s and checkout "upstream X timeout" messages are almost always symptoms; the service whose *own* error_rate rises first and highest is the culprit (payments in p-005).
5. **Deploys timed near an incident are frequently red herrings** (dep-008). Check whether the deployed service is where errors originate, and whether the degradation trend predates the deploy.

## Routine log noise (ignore, appears on healthy days)
`request body larger than 1MB`, `client disconnected before response`, `GET /product/NNN returned 404`, search `query parse error near position N`, search `empty result for filtered query`, `retrying upstream call (attempt 2/3)`, payments `card declined by issuer (code 05)`, payments `duplicate idempotency key`, checkout `cart validation failed: missing shipping zip`, inventory `stock level race detected, retried`.

## Baselines (weekday, non-batch)
web p99 ~160–205, er ~0.003, rps ~60 overnight rising to peak late morning; checkout p99 ~300–400, er ~0.002, rps ~18 overnight / 96 at 11:00; payments p99 ~210–290, er ~0.001, rps ~15 overnight / 80 at 11:00, conns ~4; inventory p99 ~110–130, er ~0.001, rps ~22.5; search p99 ~130–180, er ~0.002, cache_hit_rate ~0.92; postgres p99 6–11ms, cpu ~30%; redis p99 ~1.2–1.8ms, cpu ~18%. Weekend traffic ≈ half of weekday. Traffic ramps steeply 08:00→11:00.

## Handoff notes worth remembering
- Deploy authors seen: dana, eli, gus, hana, farah, alice (alice did the cfg-005 revert). Deploy messages are mostly generic ("clean up dead code", "improve error messages", "add request tracing spans") and carry little diagnostic signal — don't over-weight them.
- Latest changes not yet stress-tested at peak: cfg-010 (redis.maxmemory_mb 3584), cfg-011 (inventory.reservation_ttl_s 600→900, dana, day 11 15:45), dep-026 payments v2.2.4 / dep-027 web v3.12.6 (tracing spans, day 11 16:15/16:25), dep-024/025 inventory v2.7.6/v2.7.7 (day 11).
- Current versions as of end of day 11: web v3.12.6, checkout v1.4.6, payments v2.2.4, inventory v2.7.7, search v1.9.4.
- Query budget is 15/page and 50 rows/result: always aggregate with GROUP BY service / date_trunc. Three parallel queries (logs window, per-service metric aggregate, alerts window) resolve the nightly page; the p-005-style real incident took ~5 (add: deploys+config since midnight, hourly trend by service, log message counts with first/last seen).
